**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](./Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). As profession, he's head of a bank in [Ath](./Ath "Ath").[[1]](./Alexandre_Boucaut#cite_note-1)

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### First League Record

See also: [Participants of Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League#All_time_tables "Montenegrin First League")

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in Montenegrin First League on season [2006–07](./2006–07_Montenegrin_First_League "2006–07 Montenegrin First League"). Below is a list of OFK Grbalj scores in First League by every single season.

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](./Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). As profession, he's head of a bank in [Ath](./Ath "Ath").[[1]](./Alexandre_Boucaut#cite_note-1)

After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). **Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). **Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](./2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").  
They were first team from Montenegrin coastal region which played in [UEFA](./UEFA "UEFA") competitions. Until now, OFK Grbalj played two seasons in European cups.

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](./Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). As profession, he's head of a bank in [Ath](./Ath "Ath").[[1]](./Alexandre_Boucaut#cite_note-1)

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](./Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). As profession, he's head of a bank in [Ath](./Ath "Ath").[[1]](./Alexandre_Boucaut#cite_note-1)

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](./2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").  
They were first team from Montenegrin coastal region which played in [UEFA](./UEFA "UEFA") competitions. Until now, OFK Grbalj played two seasons in European cups.

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\n### First League Record\\n\\nSee also: [Participants of Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League#All_time_tables \"Montenegrin First League\")\\n\\nFor the first time, OFK Grbalj played in Montenegrin First League on season [2006–07](./2006–07_Montenegrin_First_League \"2006–07 Montenegrin First League\"). **Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](./2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").  
They were first team from Montenegrin coastal region which played in [UEFA](./UEFA "UEFA") competitions. Until now, OFK Grbalj played two seasons in European cups.

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](./Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). As profession, he's head of a bank in [Ath](./Ath "Ath").[[1]](./Alexandre_Boucaut#cite_note-1)

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](./Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). **Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Alexandre Boucaut** (born 10 August 1980) is a [Belgian](./Belgian_people "Belgian people") football referee. He made his debut in the [Belgian Pro League](./Belgian_Pro_League "Belgian Pro League") at 8 February 2009 in a game between [KVC Westerlo](./KVC_Westerlo "KVC Westerlo") and [KSC Lokeren](./KSC_Lokeren "KSC Lokeren"). **Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").
